newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Higher oil price lifts Lasmo profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Higher oil price lifts Lasmo profits.

text.p: Higher first-half crude oil prices fuelled profits for exploration and production company Lasmo Plc, which on Thursday said it expects its output to fire ahead in coming years.
"Things look quite good from an operational point of view," chief executive Joe Darby told Reuters.
Net profit rose to 26 million pounds ($42.5 million) in the first half of 1997 from 24 million pounds a year ago, coming in at the low end of analysts' expectations.
The earnings advance was dampened by the pound's strength, which meant that a nine percent dollar increase in crude oil prices translated in a mere two percent rise in sterling terms.
The oil price averaged $19.40 per barrel in the first six months compared with $17.82 in the same 1996 period.
Lasmo, Britain's second biggest exploration and production company, said it did not expect oil prices to change much in the next few months.
If anything there could be some weakness, Darby said, pointing to any further Iraqi oil exports.
There might also be some price pressure from increased production worldwide as oil fields were coming back to full capacity following the traditional summer maintenance period, he added.

Lasmo's own production remained flat at 171,000 barrels per day in the first six months of 1997. But the company sees a second half increase as the North Sea MacCulloch field may come onstream any day now.

The field, in which Lasmo has a 40 percent interest, was originally scheduled to start up in January. But mechanical problems at the production vessel and extra time needed to hook up facilities led to a delay.

Darby said the first half of 1997 had nonetheless been successful, pointing to four discoveries in Algeria, a significant gas discovery in Pakistan and the $453 million oil contract in Venezuela, which was won last month.
"That provides us with solid baseline production," Darby said.
He expects Lasmo's output to grow to about 250,000 barrels per day by 2001.
This outlook helped Lasmo shares gain 10-1/2 pence to 279 in a volatile market, one analyst said.

"For the first time they gave us an explicit target," said Irene Himona at SocGen. But another industry watcher was more sceptical, saying a technical short squeeze was the main motor behind the share rise. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
